display.purpose: Short brand statements and the home headline; the custom Daisy wordmark remains artwork.

headline.purpose: Section heads, the native statement, and closing statements.

body.purpose: Plain product and usage copy at a 65–75ch measure.

label.purpose: Compact macOS controls and explicit state labels.

mono.purpose: Code blocks and inline code on white or Paper Raised surfaces.

shadows.name: app-icon-tile
shadows.purpose: Soft native depth for the app-icon tile only; never apply to the flower or chain.

motion.name: state-color
motion.purpose: Optional connected-to-disconnected color transition; reduced motion may switch instantly.

motion.name: web-ease-out
motion.purpose: Website hover and press transitions on links, buttons, and desk controls; reduced motion collapses it.

motion.name: display-spring
motion.purpose: Desk displays spring to place, snap to a neighbour within 56 units, and settle with a small overshoot; the loop sleeps once settled.

motion.name: chain-rope
motion.purpose: Desk chains as Verlet ropes of rigid closed links that rest nearly straight and re-link rather than stretch.

motion.name: chain-pull
motion.purpose: On a control crossing, a pull passes joint by joint toward the target, whose flower blooms.

motion.name: thread-link-in
motion.purpose: Thread links scale in place as they scroll into view and retract on scroll back; reduced motion shows them complete.

motion.name: thread-flower-connect
motion.value: center fill 0.5s, petals rotate 22.5deg over 0.6s, cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)
motion.purpose: A thread flower turns gray to yellow and turns its petals when the chain reaches it.

components.name: Connected Menu Status
components.description: The flower alone; yellow center is the only connected-state cue.
components.css: .ds-menu-flower { display: inline-flex; width: 24px; height: 24px; } .ds-menu-flower svg { width: 100%; height: 100%; overflow: visible; } .ds-menu-flower .petals { fill: #737D84; } .ds-menu-flower .center { fill: #FFD447; transition: fill 160ms cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1); }

components.name: Disconnected Menu Status
components.description: The identical flower silhouette with a gray center and no link ears.
components.css: .ds-menu-flower { display: inline-flex; width: 24px; height: 24px; } .ds-menu-flower svg { width: 100%; height: 100%; overflow: visible; } .ds-menu-flower .petals { fill: #737D84; } .ds-menu-flower .center { fill: #A3A7AA; transition: fill 160ms cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1); }

components.name: Horizontal Daisy Chain Node
components.description: A centered flower with the nearest curved U-link bowls facing it.
components.css: .ds-chain-node { display: inline-flex; width: 220px; max-width: 100%; } .ds-chain-node svg { width: 100%; height: auto; } .ds-chain-node .link { fill: none; stroke: #737D84; stroke-width: 9; stroke-linecap: round; stroke-linejoin: round; } .ds-chain-node .flower { fill: #2E3235; } .ds-chain-node .center { fill: #FFD447; }

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Graphite pill for the one main action, such as Download.

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Transparent pill with an inset hairline for secondary actions.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; padding: 0.85rem 1.35rem; border-radius: 999px; background: transparent; color: #2E3235; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px #C7C8C4; font: 600 1rem/1.1 -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Text', sans-serif; text-decoration: none; transition: background-color 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background: #EFEEE9; } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #2E3235; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Planned Chip
components.description: Graphite pill marking a feature that is planned, not shipped.
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-block; font: 600 0.72rem/1.2 -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Text', sans-serif; padding: 0.25em 0.55em; border-radius: 999px; background: #2E3235; color: #F7F6F2; }

components.name: Code Block
components.description: White code surface with monochrome highlighting: graphite, Secondary Ink, Code Muted.
components.html:
# verify the release
shasum -a 256 Daisy-0.1.0.zip
components.css: .ds-code { margin: 0; padding: 1.1rem 1.25rem; background: #FFFFFF; border: 1px solid #DDDCD5; border-radius: 12px; overflow-x: auto; font: 0.875rem/1.6 ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', Menlo, monospace; color: #2E3235; } .ds-code .k { color: #2E3235; } .ds-code .s { color: #4F565B; } .ds-code .c { color: #6A7379; }

components.name: Header Navigation
components.description: Secondary Ink label links; the current page is graphite and underlined.
components.css: .ds-nav { display: flex; gap: 1.5rem; list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; font: 500 0.9375rem/1.2 -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Text', sans-serif; } .ds-nav a { color: #4F565B; text-decoration: none; padding-block: 6px; text-underline-offset: 0.22em; } .ds-nav a:hover, .ds-nav a[aria-current=page] { color: #2E3235; } .ds-nav a[aria-current=page] { text-decoration: underline; text-decoration-color: #2E3235; } .ds-nav a:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #2E3235; outline-offset: 3px; border-radius: 4px; }

components.name: Coral Display Phrase
components.description: One display phrase per page underlined in coral; the text stays graphite.

components.description: Stand-in for artwork awaiting the image pass, at the final aspect ratio.
components.css: .ds-ph { margin: 0; width: 100%; border: 1px dashed #B3B6B6; border-radius: 14px; background: repeating-linear-gradient(135deg, transparent 0 14px, rgba(46, 50, 53, 0.045) 14px 15px), #EFEEE9; display: grid; place-items: center; padding: 1.5rem; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Text', sans-serif; } .ds-ph figcaption { display: grid; gap: 0.35rem; justify-items: center; text-align: center; max-width: 46ch; color: #4F565B; font-size: 0.9375rem; } .ds-ph-tag { font-size: 0.72rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.04em; padding: 0.25em 0.6em; border-radius: 999px; border: 1px dashed #9EA2A3; } .ds-ph-subject { font-weight: 600; color: #2E3235; } .ds-ph-spec { font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-ph-alt { font-size: 0.85rem; }

narrative.overview: Daisy turns separate Macs into one quiet, continuous workspace. A centered flower gives each Mac equal weight, while repeated fixed-size U links imply an open-ended chain. Warm off-white, graphite, matte anodized gray, precise connection yellow, and restrained coral keep complexity optional and status immediate. The website's vector marks are interim drawings of these rules; production artwork replaces the shapes, not the rules.
keyCharacteristics: One centered Daisy node per Mac.
Open-ended chains built from repeating fixed-size U links that may turn and flow at angles.
Flat matte metal links, never black or glossy.
Color-only connected and disconnected menu-bar states.
A flower-only app icon for clean small-scale recognition.

rules.name: The Yellow Signal Rule
rules.body: Yellow appears only at the center of a connected Daisy.

rules.name: The Matte Metal Rule
rules.body: U links use one flat anodized-gray value with no sheen, highlight, gradient, gloss, or simulated texture.

rules.name: The Coral Restraint Rule
rules.body: Coral is a secondary editorial accent, never a link, field, or status color.

rules.name: The Coral Underline Rule
rules.body: Coral never fills text: it measures 2.6:1 on Daisy Paper. Emphasize at most one display phrase per page with a thick coral underline (thickness 0.09em, offset 0.12em, skip-ink off) beneath graphite text.

rules.name: The Secondary Ink Rule
rules.body: Secondary text is Secondary Ink (6.9:1 on paper), never Anodized Link, which measures 3.9:1 and fails AA for body text. Anodized gray is for links, strokes, and marks.

rules.name: The Monochrome Code Rule
rules.body: Code highlighting uses no hue: keywords, functions, parameters, and plain text in graphite; strings and constants in Secondary Ink; comments and punctuation in Code Muted (4.8:1 on white, 4.5:1 on paper, so valid only on the white code surface).

rules.name: The Native Voice Rule
rules.body: Product UI uses the macOS system typeface; custom display lettering belongs to the Daisy wordmark.

rules.name: The Flat Chain Rule
rules.body: Links never gain depth, bevels, inner shadows, or glow.

rules.name: The Flowing Chain Rule
rules.body: A chain may change direction from link to link; every turn uses rotated, overlapping copies of the same U geometry, never a smooth connector or distorted link.

rules.name: The Chain Spacing Rule
rules.body: A run between two flowers alternates ⊂⊃⊂⊃ with an even link count, so the link nearest each flower has its bowl toward that flower. Facing tips overlap about 6 units and back-to-back bowls about 5. When the distance is not an exact fit, tighten every joint equally by up to 14 units so the run reaches from flower to flower; past that, drop a pair. Keep about 44 units of clearance around each flower. Links stay one flat color so overlapping facing tips close into ovals; shading or a second color would expose the seam.

rules.name: The Placeholder Rule
rules.body: Artwork awaiting the image pass ships as a placeholder figure at its final aspect ratio, never an invented stand-in image. It has a dashed #B3B6B6 border, 14px corners, and a faint 135° hairline hatch over Paper Raised, centering a caption stack: a dashed Placeholder pill, the subject in semibold graphite, the ratio and pixel size in tabular figures, and the intended alt text. The figure is role="img", labelled with that alt text. A missing wordmark uses the same dashed, hatched treatment at its final size.

rules.name: The Rigid Link Rule
rules.body: Each segment of a moving chain is one closed link: a ⊂⊃ pair at fixed spacing, drawn along the segment's own direction. Joints sit where neighbouring bowls overlap, so the chain never opens at a bend, and no link ever stretches, skews, or tapers in motion.

rules.name: The Taut Chain Rule
rules.body: A resting chain hangs nearly straight from flower to flower, with about 0.4% slack under gravity 700 and damping 0.985. When displays move and the slack passes about 1.5%, or the span outgrows the chain, the chain re-links to a new link count instead of drooping or stretching.

rules.name: The Pull Rule
rules.body: When control crosses to another Mac, a pull passes along the chain joint by joint, about 22ms apart, and the target flower blooms. The pull moves links; it never lengthens them.

rules.name: The Magnet Spring Rule
rules.body: Arranged displays move on springs (stiffness 340, damping ratio 0.7), snap magnetically to a neighbour within 56 units, and settle with a small overshoot. The view eases to the new bounds and follows a display while it is dragged. The animation loop sleeps once everything has settled.

rules.name: The Connect-on-Arrival Rule
rules.body: A thread flower starts disconnected, with a Disconnected Gray center. When the chain reaches it, the center turns Connection Yellow and the petals rotate 22.5°. The yellow still obeys the Yellow Signal Rule: it means that section's flower is connected. Links scale in place from 0.55 to full size as they scroll into view and retract on scroll back; they never stretch along the path.

rules.name: The Complete Thread Rule
rules.body: With reduced motion the thread shows complete: every link in place and every flower connected. Below 1100px the rail and section flowers are absent, and the Download flower shows connected.

dos: Center one flower within every depicted display.
Keep every U link identical in size, weight, color, and corner character.
Aim every curved bowl toward its adjacent flower.
Create chain length through overlapping repetition.
Let chain paths bend and flow by rotating whole links at each turn.
Use the flower alone where icon scale cannot carry the chain cleanly.
Treat the approved comp as the north star while allowing production art to improve contours and optical spacing.
Set secondary text in Secondary Ink.
Mark missing artwork with the placeholder figure at its final aspect ratio.
Move chains as rigid closed links that re-link rather than stretch.
Light a thread flower only when the chain has reached it.
Show the thread and desk in their finished state when reduced motion is requested.
donts: Reduce Daisy to two computers joined by one line.
Use hub-and-spoke, wireless arcs, network graphs, or settings imagery as the identity.
Stretch a U link into a cable, capsule, bar, or wavy connector.
Force every chain into a straight line or distort a link to fake a turn.
Point a link's open tips toward the flower.
Make links black, glossy, shaded, gradient-filled, coral, or yellow.
Add side-link ears to the menu-bar glyph or app icon.
Use a yellow field; yellow is reserved for connected centers.
Set text in coral or in anodized gray.
Open a chain at a bend or lengthen a link to absorb motion.
